lines.text: When you stop eating, how many hours does it take before your body actually starts burning body fat?
For the first four hours after a meal, your cells run entirely on digested glucose from your bloodstream.
Between hours four and twelve, insulin levels drop and your liver releases stored glycogen.
Only after twelve to fourteen hours of fasting does your body exhaust easy glycogen reserves.
Your metabolism flips the biological metabolic switch, breaking down adipose tissue into fatty acids.
By hour sixteen, ketones flood your bloodstream to fuel your brain with razor-sharp focus.
Intermittent fasting simply allows your ancient fat-burning engine time to turn on.
